content.value_statement: Teams often ship prompts without clear evaluation, structure, or operating guidance. This skill provides practical patterns for prompt design, RAG review, and agent planning.
actual_capabilities: Documents prompt engineering patterns for production LLM workflows.
Provides references for LLM evaluation, RAG review, and agentic system design.
Includes placeholder Python CLI scripts for optimization, evaluation, and orchestration workflows.
Lists production concerns such as monitoring, security, reliability, and cost.
Supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code assisted development workflows.
limitations: The included Python scripts are scaffold examples and need project-specific implementation.
Some documented command examples require adaptation before use.
The skill does not call model APIs or run evaluations automatically.
Results depend on the user providing task goals, constraints, and evaluation criteria.

use_cases.title: Improve Product Prompts
use_cases.description: Turn loose feature prompts into structured instructions with goals, constraints, examples, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Design Evaluation Plans
use_cases.description: Create practical checks for prompt quality, RAG behavior, failure modes, and production readiness.

use_cases.title: Plan Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Outline agent roles, tool boundaries, observability needs, and deployment considerations for AI systems.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Prompt Goal
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt for clarity. Identify the user goal, missing context, confusing wording, and three concrete improvements: [paste prompt].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Structured Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a production prompt for [task]. Include role, inputs, output format, constraints, examples, and refusal boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Evaluation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an evaluation plan for [LLM feature]. Include success criteria, test cases, edge cases, scoring guidance, and review cadence.

prompt_templates.title: Architect an Agentic Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an agent workflow for [business process]. Define agent responsibilities, tool access, memory policy, monitoring, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: A support chatbot prompt needs better consistency and safer answers.
output: A revised prompt with clear role, tone, allowed sources, and escalation rules.
A test plan covering policy questions, ambiguous requests, and unsupported claims.
A short checklist for measuring answer accuracy and refusal quality.

output_examples.input: A RAG assistant returns answers that are detailed but poorly grounded.
output: A diagnosis of retrieval, context selection, citation, and answer synthesis risks.
A prompt structure that separates evidence review from final response writing.
Evaluation cases for missing context, conflicting sources, and low-confidence answers.

output_examples.input: A team wants to plan a multi-step agent for internal operations.
output: A workflow map with agent responsibilities, tool boundaries, and approval points.
Operational requirements for logging, monitoring, access control, and fallback handling.
A risk checklist for unwanted actions, stale context, and unclear ownership.

best_practices: Start with the task goal, user context, constraints, and evaluation criteria.
Use examples that reflect real edge cases and expected output quality.
Review tool access, data handling, and fallback behavior before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on vague role prompts without measurable success criteria.
Do not expose broad tool access without clear approval and logging rules.
Do not treat one successful model response as proof of production readiness.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create structured prompts, evaluation plans, RAG review guidance, and agent workflow plans.

faq.question: Does it run prompt evaluations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and scaffold scripts, but users must implement project-specific evaluation logic.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is this only for prompt engineers?
faq.answer: No. Product managers, AI engineers, and platform teams can use it for planning and review.

faq.question: Does it include production security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It references access control, data handling, audit logging, monitoring, and deployment review topics.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the target task, user needs, model constraints, example inputs, and quality requirements.
